text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- A new draft law to check adulteration in petroleum products is likely to be approved in three weeks.
- A government committee has approved a 90 billion rupees Public Sector Development Programme for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June), which is 14 billion lower than the original programme.
- The Export Promotion Bureau has decided to disallow spot sale by exporters participating in single-country exhibitions and trade fairs abroad.
THE NEWS

- The United States has expressed its strong concern over the detention of a Pakistani employee of the Drug Enforment Agency office of the U.S. embassy in Islamabad, Ayaz Baluch, and urged Pakistan to release him.

- More than 100 people were injured in a violent clash between prisoners belonging to (the militant Shi'ite group) Sipah-i-Mohammad and police in Adiala jail, near Rawalpindi. Some barracks were also set on fire, which destroyed prison record and furniture.

- The Federal Investigation Agency has sent to all its offices in Pakistan a list of 123 people, including former prime minister Benazir Bhutto, with instructions to provide their "identifying particulars" to place their names on the Exit Control List.
- Twenty-six people died in Astore valley on Saturday as meningitis broke out in two small villages there. The death toll may rise as 160 more people were also affected by the disease.
THE NATION

- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has said in an interview that trade relations with India will be possible if there is a visible progress in the resolution of Kashmir dispute, India withdraws its "occupation forces" from Kashmir and stops "a reign of terror" let loose there.
- The federal government, under the directives of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, is launcing a vigorous drive to recover illegal arms from all over Pakistan to restore law and order.
- THE MUSLIM

- Alarmed by the serious downslide of economy, coupled with fast deterioration of the law and order situation in the country, the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee, at its meeting in Rawalpindi on Saturday, observed with deep concern that the present conditions could pose a serious threat to Pakistan's external and internal security.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Top bankers have proposed to the government to impose a ban on trade union activities for an effective and smooth implementation of restructuring and down-sizing programme.
FINANCIAL POST
- Information Technology Market, 97 (INTECHMART '97) was launched in Pakistan on Saturday.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
